description: Cumulus is a squad of six first-year engineering students turning complex space data into an intuitive, visual experience. From 3D lunar mapping to backend data integration, we’re combining fresh perspectives and hands-on coding to help users navigate the next frontier of Moon missions.
summary: SELENE-3D is an interactive 3D lunar atlas that helps students, educators, and mission planners explore the Moon and understand where it is safe to land. Inspired by NASA Moon Trek and LROC QuickMap, it renders a detailed 3D Moon in the browser with switchable views of natural surface, LOLA-style elevation, and shaded relief. Users can fly to landing sites, from Apollo 11 to Chandrayaan-3, Chang’e 4, and Artemis III candidate regions, and open telemetry cards with coordinates, elevation, and mission details. A solar phase simulator shows how lighting and shadows change across the lunar day, while terrain tools filter the surface by elevation, slope, and roughness to highlight flat, low-hazard areas. A live cursor readout reports latitude, longitude, and elevation, and a search tool and keyboard shortcuts make navigation quick. SELENE-3D addresses a major challenge: lunar mission data is spread across complex, specialist tools that are hard to explore. By bringing it into one visual, interactive experience built with React and Three.js, it makes landing site analysis faster and more accessible.
details:
SELENE-3D is a production-ready, interactive 3D lunar exploration web application inspired by NASA Moon Trek and LROC QuickMap, powered by React, Three.js, and TypeScript, it combines high-resolution lunar terrain mapping, real-time solar lighting simulation, and scientific LOLA elevation analysis with interactive tools for exploring landing sites, comparing locations, and evaluating mission feasibility. 

How does it work?

SELENE-3D is an interactive, browser-based 3D geospatial engine built with React, Three.js, and TypeScript that transforms NASA lunar datasets into a real-time mission planning workspace. Powered by custom WebGL shaders, it renders a high-resolution Moon globe capable of dynamically switching between LROC visual mosaics, LOLA elevation maps, and shaded relief layers. As users explore or hover over the surface, a real-time raycasting engine converts 3D coordinates into live latitude/longitude, elevation, slope, and roughness metrics on the HUD. Users can simulate day/night shadows via a 360° solar phase controller, launch 3D flyover tours to Apollo, Chandrayaan-3, and Artemis III sites, and use integrated tools—like the Lunar Site Comparator, Celestial Horizon, and Mission Evaluator—to assess landing safety, solar power, and Earth communication windows.

Benefits:

  • Rapid, Agile Mission Planning: Replaces slow, fragmented desktop GIS workflows with an instant, browser-based 3D workspace. Using the Lunar Site Comparator and Mission Evaluator, planners can compare candidate sites side-by-side and adapt quickly when launch windows, schedules, or hardware requirements change.
  • Clear Solar Power & Communication Assessments: Solves the biggest challenges of lunar south pole exploration—extreme shadows and intermittent line-of-sight. Through the Celestial Horizon simulator and Solar Phase & Lighting controls, users can visualize Sun and Earth positions relative to the local horizon to evaluate solar power generation potential and direct-to-Earth communication windows.
  • Data-Driven Landing Safety: Translates complex NASA LOLA elevation and SLDEM datasets into clear, visual safety metrics—allowing teams to filter out dangerous steep slopes (>15°), rough crater terrain, and deep shadow zones before committing to a landing zone.
  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility Across Skill Levels: Bridges the gap between technical engineering data and public understanding. Mission analysts get real-time DMS coordinates, slope angles, and RMS surface roughness on hover, while students and educators can explore why small shifts in location or date drastically impact lunar missions using 3D Flyover Tours and historical mission cards (Apollo, Chandrayaan-3, Artemis III).
  • Unified Multi-Dataset Visualization: Combines photographic LROC mosaics, hypsometric elevation maps, shaded relief, and horizon geometry into one cohesive, zero-install web application. 

Intended impact:

SELENE-3D bridges the gap between raw, complex planetary datasets and agile lunar mission planning. Missions to the Moon—especially the South Pole—face extreme lighting, steep terrain, and strict communication constraints. By translating NASA LOLA elevation data, solar lighting simulations, and horizon visibility into an intuitive 3D interface, SELENE-3D empowers:

  • Agile Mission Planning: Enables engineers and planners to rapidly compare candidate landing sites, evaluate slope and surface roughness safety, and assess solar power generation and direct-to-Earth communication feasibility—helping teams quickly adapt when launch windows or hardware requirements shift.
  • Public & STEM Education: Makes complex orbital mechanics and lunar geography accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts through interactive 3D flyover tours, real-time day/night phase controls, and historical mission telemetry (from Apollo to Chandrayaan-3 and Artemis III)

Tech Stack and Tools:

  • Core Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, and custom WebGL / GLSL shaders 
  • Frontend & 3D Graphics: React 18, Three.js, Tailwind CSS, Figma
  • Build Tools: Vite 5 and Node.js / npm. 
  • Deployment: Deployed via Vercel
  • Video editing: VN Editor(Microsoft clipchamp)

Creativity and innovation:

SELENE-3D reimagines traditional, complex planetary GIS software as an intuitive, zero-install 3D mission control interface directly in the browser. Instead of forcing users to cross-reference static maps and raw spreadsheets, we fused real-time WebGL terrain shaders, dynamic solar phase simulation, and live cursor raycasting into a single cohesive workspace. Our standout innovation lies in translating intricate orbital and geodetic physics—such as Celestial Horizon Sun/Earth line-of-sight geometry, Horn’s slope safety algorithms, and dual-location comparisons via the Lunar Site Comparator—into instant visual feedback, empowering both mission planners and everyday learners to see how slight changes in landing coordinates or dates impact lunar power, communications, and safety. 

On the whole, SELENE-3D transforms raw NASA lunar datasets into an accessible, real-time 3D mission control interface directly in the browser. By bridging the gap between complex planetary geodesy and intuitive visual exploration, it equips both mission planners and future explorers with the tools needed to navigate the Moon safely—paving the way for sustainable lunar exploration.

 

Use of AI tools:

  • Gemini - It was used for AI voiceover and for research and brainstorming as well.
